pageInfo.subtitle: Master wide intervallic leaps, arpeggio jumping, angular modern phrasing, and fretboard-spanning agility without pick snags.
pageInfo.heroDescription: String skipping is the definitive technique for breaking out of linear, scalar rut playing and injecting vocal, horn-like intervallic leaps into your guitar vocabulary. By deliberately vaulting over one or two unplayed strings, you create wide-interval arpeggios, wide octave jumps, and angular modern melodic contours impossible with standard adjacent-string picking. Pioneered by virtuosos like Paul Gilbert, Guthrie Govan, Greg Howe, and Buckethead, mastering string skipping requires surgical pick-trajectory arching, sympathetic damping of intervening strings, and synchronized fretting-hand muting.

items.text: The Curvilinear Pick Arc: Never travel diagonally across skipped strings. Use a subtle micro-arc trajectory that lifts the pick tip slightly away from the soundboard to vault cleanly over the idle string.
Directional Pick Slanting: Employ downward pick slanting when skipping downwards and upward pick slanting when skipping upwards to ensure the pick escapes the string bed without catching.
Right-Hand Spatial Anchor: Keep the fleshy heel of your picking palm resting lightly along the bridge saddle to maintain an absolute spatial reference frame for wide string leaps.

Strict Alternate vs. Outside Picking: Standardize your picking logic. Initiating string skips with outside pick strokes (downstroke on lower string, upstroke on higher string) generally provides maximum clearance.
Metronome Subdivisions: Avoid the common trap of rushing the jump. Practice with a rigid metronome click on every 16th or 8th note so the skipped distance does not distort your rhythm.
Underside Index Finger Muting: Lay the soft underside flesh of your index finger gently across the skipped intermediate string to choke accidental pick contact or sympathetic harmonic vibration.
Linear Arpeggio Deconstruction: Convert standard 5- and 6-string sweep shapes into 2-string-pair skipped shapes (e.g., strings 6 & 4, 5 & 3) to produce articulate, pianistic arpeggios.
Intervallic Ear Conditioning: Train your ear to expect 6ths, 7ths, and 9ths rather than stepwise 2nds. String skipping turns guitar lines into trumpet- and saxophone-like melodic leaps.
Legato String-Skip Integration: Combine hammer-ons and pull-offs on each string with a single pick stroke per string to achieve fluid velocity with minimal right-hand fatigue.
Lateral Position Shifting: When navigating diagonal fretboard runs, coordinate the fretting hand shift during the string skip so your hand lands precisely on target without hesitation.

exercises.title: The One-String Gap: Octave Jumps (Strings 6 & 4)
exercises.description: Establish the foundational micro-arc pick trajectory by leaping over the 5th string to play root-octave pairs between the 6th and 4th strings. Ensure string 5 is completely silenced by the index finger underside.

patternNote.text: Mechanic: Vault pick cleanly over string 5; mute string 5 with index finger flesh

notation.title: One-String Gap: Octave Leaps Across Strings 6 and 4

practiceNotes.title: Practice Notes
practiceNotes.text: Use strict alternate picking: downstroke on the 6th string, upstroke on the 4th string (outside picking). The pick must lift just enough to clear string 5 without wasting vertical motion.

exercises.title: Two-String Gap: 10th Interval Jumps (Strings 6 & 3)
exercises.description: Double the leap distance by vaulting across strings 5 and 4 to strike beautiful major and minor 10ths on string 3. This wide intervallic motion is the secret behind Eric Johnson and modern fusion chords.

patternNote.text: Intervals: Wide 10ths leaping across two unpicked intermediate strings

practiceNotes.title: Practice Notes
practiceNotes.text: With two strings between your pick targets, your picking wrist must maintain absolute spatial calibration. Keep your palm heel anchored lightly on the lower bridge edge.

exercises.title: Pentatonic String-Skip Sequences (A Minor Box 1)
exercises.description: Transform the familiar A minor pentatonic box 1 into an angular, unpredictable lead sequence by skipping alternating string sets: string 6 to string 4, then string 5 to string 3, then string 4 to string 2.

patternNote.text: Shape: A minor pentatonic sequenced with string-skipping pairs

practiceNotes.title: Practice Notes
practiceNotes.text: Notice how skipping strings eliminates the predictable scalar sound of box 1. Maintain consistent 16th-note subdivision; do not rush the string transitions.

exercises.title: Paul Gilbert Arpeggio Skip (Am & C Major)
exercises.description: The quintessential Paul Gilbert shred arpeggio: play 3 notes on the 5th string using hammer-on and pull-off, leap over string 4, and strike the triad completion on string 3. Crystal clear, percussive, and blazing fast.

patternNote.text: Technique: Legato 3-note burst on string 5 + skipped single note on string 3

practiceNotes.title: Practice Notes
practiceNotes.text: Pick the first note on string 5 (downstroke), hammer to 15, pull-off back to 12, then upstroke the note on string 3. This allows blistering 16th-note arpeggio cascades with only 2 pick strokes per group.

sections.title: Virtuoso Application: Modern Legato & Complex Harmony

exercises.title: Diatonic 3-Octave Scale Skips in G Major
exercises.description: Ascend through the G major diatonic scale by skipping alternate strings across two complete octaves. This exercise trains both pick accuracy and large fretting-hand lateral position shifts.

patternNote.text: Harmony: G Major diatonic run with strings 6->4, 5->3, 4->2, 3->1

notation.title: Diatonic Multi-Octave Scale Skips in G Major

practiceNotes.title: Practice Notes
practiceNotes.text: Notice the recurring mechanical pattern: play two notes on the lower string, skip a string, and play two notes on the higher string. Keep the wrist relaxed and use small, economical pick motions.

exercises.title: Jazz-Fusion Cadence Arpeggios (Dm7 - G7 - Cmaj7)
exercises.description: Outline a standard ii-V-I jazz cadence using string-skipping arpeggios. By jumping over intermediate strings, chord tones speak with pristine voice leading and open acoustic width.

patternNote.text: Progression: Dm7 (ii) -> G7 (V) -> Cmaj7 (I) with skipped chord tones

notation.title: String-Skipping Jazz Cadence: Dm7 - G7 - Cmaj7

practiceNotes.title: Practice Notes
practiceNotes.text: Listen carefully to the voice leading. The wide intervals outline 7th chords with sophisticated, horn-like transparency that avoids guitaristic cliches.

exercises.title: The Guthrie Govan Master Etude: Wide Legato Skips
exercises.description: The ultimate test of modern string-skipping mastery: wide, 3-octave E Dorian arpeggio runs that vault across strings 6, 4, 2 and 5, 3, 1 using high-velocity legato and pinpoint pick strikes.

patternNote.text: Virtuoso Etude: E Dorian multi-octave string-skipping cascades

notation.title: Guthrie Govan E Dorian Master String-Skipping Etude

practiceNotes.title: Practice Notes
practiceNotes.text: Execute this etude with zero unwanted string noise. Your index finger underside and right-hand palm heel must work in continuous tandem to silence unplayed strings as you vault across the fretboard.

items.title: 3 Mistakes That Kill Your String Skipping
items: Flat Pick Trajectory (The Snag): Moving the pick straight across the fretboard plane causes the pick tip to collide violently with the skipped string. You must cultivate a micro-arc that lifts cleanly over unplayed strings.
Sympathetic Drone from the Idle String: Failing to drape your fretting index finger or picking palm over the skipped string creates discordant, unwanted ringing that turns fast runs into mush.

Tensing the Forearm on Wide Jumps: As string gaps widen from 1 to 2 strings, players instinctively stiffen their arm muscles. Maintain a relaxed wrist and fluid forearm rotation to preserve endurance.

items.title: Masters of String Skipping
items: Paul Gilbert: The godfather of high-speed string-skipping arpeggios; proved in Racer X and Mr. Big that skipping strings offers sharper attack and superior clarity over sweep picking.
Guthrie Govan: Modern fusion maestro who uses string skipping to execute complex, multi-octave horn lines and impossible intervallic shifts with effortless legato.
Buckethead: Blends blazing string-skipping arpeggios, wide-interval octave jumps, and robotic precision across avant-garde metal and shred albums.
Greg Howe: Pioneer of funky, syncopated fusion string skipping; integrates two-handed tapping and hammer-ons from nowhere across non-adjacent strings.

items.title: The 15-Minute Daily String-Skipping Workout
items: Block 1: Micro-Arc Octave Clearance (5 min) - Cycle Exercise 1 between strings 6 & 4, and 5 & 3 at 75 BPM, focusing on total silence on the skipped string.
Block 2: Gilbert Arpeggio Burst Cycles (5 min) - Practice the Paul Gilbert A minor and C major patterns at 90 BPM, syncing the hammer-pull with the outside pick stroke.
Block 3: Full-Neck Traversal Etude (5 min) - Run the Guthrie Govan E Dorian etude across multiple fret positions, maintaining strict metronome lock and relaxed breathing.
